chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Mansur ibn Yunus from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah: A man said to me: 'Know the last one of the Imams and it does not harm you if you have not known the first one.' He said: 'May Allah curse him! I hate him although I do not know him. Has the last one been known except by knowing the first one?'

key_terms.الْآخِرُ: The last one (referring to the final Imam)
key_terms.الْأَوَّلُ: The first one (referring to the first Imam)

ai.seo_question: Why is knowing the first Imam necessary to know the last Imam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) pronounces a curse on the one who claims to know the final Imam while ignoring the first, emphasizing that the validity of the later Imams is contingent upon the recognition of the earlier ones. This hadith underscores the Shia doctrine of the continuity of the Imamate, where the 'Last' (al-Akhir) is defined by his lineage and authority flowing from the 'First' (al-Awwal), making the rejection of any link in the chain a rejection of the whole. It serves as a critical theological argument against those who might accept the concept of an Imam without adhering to the specific, unbroken line of twelve successors.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (9) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya from Ahmad bin Muhammad from Muhammad bin Issma’eel from Mansoor bin Younus that Muhammad bin Muslim had said:

I said to Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) that someone had said to me: “Know the last one of the imams and it does not harm you if you have not known the first one of them.” Imam as-Sadiq (as) said: “May Allah damn him! I hate him although I do not know him. Has the last one of them been known except by knowing the first one?”
